newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares slip, snared in narrow range.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares slip, snared in narrow range.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange fell 0.18 percent on Wednesday, ending the trading week still entrenched in the tight range which snared the market in early October.

The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.26 points to 147.61 points in moderate trade worth 429,000 dinars ($606,000), dominated by a couple of block transactions between investors, brokers said.

The index has spent past seven weeks stuck within a point either side of 147.7 points, and brokers say there is little sign of it breaking out before a series of laws governing companies and the Amman exchange itself go before parliament.
Palestinian-Israeli stalemate over troop redeployment in Hebron and doubts that Iraq will export oil at all this year are also weighing on the market.
Arab Banking Corporation dominated trade with a turnover of 135,000 dinars, one third of Wednesday's volume, but brokers said it was a private reshuffling of portfolios by investors.
"Only about 100,000 dinars worth of shares were traded openly on the floor today," one broker said.
Three shares rose, Middle East Hotels, Jordan Gulf Bank and Arab Potash. But they accounted for just 6,000 dinars turnover between them and failed to stem the tide of 27 falling shares.
Stocks in another seven companies traded but closed unchanged.
